title: Swedish Housing Law — Use, Conduct, Access and Transfer Expansion
purpose: Add tenant care and conduct, landlord access, transfer and exchange paths from Chapter 12 without collapsing statutory reasonableness standards into automatic outcomes.

sections.summary: The tenant must care for the apartment, can be liable for damage caused by fault/negligence by the tenant or persons for whom the tenant is responsible, and must notify the landlord of urgent damage or defects under the statutory timing rules.
The tenant must preserve safety, health, order and good condition in the property and must not expose neighbours to disturbances beyond what they reasonably should tolerate.

For ordinary poor conduct or disturbances the landlord must call on the tenant to stop immediately and, for residential tenancy, notify the municipal social welfare committee; specially serious cases follow a different path.
The tenant must closely supervise persons for whom the tenant is responsible so they do not engage in poor conduct or housing disturbances.

The landlord has a statutory right to prompt access for necessary inspection of the apartment or its use and for urgent improvements; other works and showings follow additional notice and inconvenience rules.

The tenant may not transfer the tenancy without landlord consent unless another statutory transfer route applies. Unreasonable refusal or no response within three weeks gives the tenant a termination route.

A residential tenant who will no longer use the apartment may obtain tribunal permission to transfer the tenancy to a close relative with whom the tenant has permanently cohabited, if the landlord can reasonably accept the change.

Tribunal permission for a residential exchange requires noteworthy reasons and no material inconvenience to the landlord; prohibited compensation prevents permission, and residence shorter than one year requires exceptional reasons.
After an authorized transfer the outgoing tenant is generally free from obligations for the later period, subject to conditions and specified pre-transfer liabilities.

rules.explanation: The represented facts state negligence by the tenant or a person within the tenant's statutory responsibility sphere, activating the Chapter 12 section 24 damage-liability path.
Urgent damage or defects must be reported immediately under section 24; additional liability still depends on what loss the notification failure caused.
Ordinary disturbances are an evaluative and procedural path: tolerability, warning, social-welfare notice and rectification must all be considered before forfeiture can be treated as established.

The represented facts include disturbance, warning, social-welfare notice and failure to rectify, activating the ordinary disturbance forfeiture route while the statutory minor-significance/proportionality safeguards remain separate.
Specially serious disturbances follow the statutory exception to the ordinary prior-warning route; other statutory safeguards remain distinct.
Refusal of access required under section 26 without a valid excuse is a represented forfeiture ground under section 42.
Section 43 prevents eviction on the represented access-refusal ground when rectification occurred before landlord termination.
Section 32 provides the general rule that transfer requires landlord consent unless a specific statutory transfer route applies.
A landlord refusal without reasonable cause activates the tenant's statutory termination route under section 32.
No landlord response within three weeks after a consent request activates the section 32 tenant termination route.
Transfer to a close relative with permanent cohabitation still requires the statutory assessment of whether the landlord can reasonably accept the new tenant.
The represented facts include close relationship, permanent cohabitation and reasonable landlord acceptance; tribunal permission remains the formal statutory route.
Residential exchange is a multi-factor permission question; the robot keeps reasons, landlord inconvenience, prohibited compensation and residence duration explicit.
The represented facts satisfy the ordinary section 35 exchange criteria and the one-year residence condition; formal tribunal permission remains required.
Where either exchange party has lived in the apartment for less than one year, section 35 requires exceptional reasons; the robot does not infer those reasons.
